To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SIRT1 is a novel therapeutic target for the prevention of renal and retinal injuries in diabetes.
In diabetes, glucose reduces SIRT1 expression in ECs, causing endothelial dysfunction and renal injury through ET‐1 and fibrotic changes through TGF‐β.
SIRT1 reduction causes diabetic renal and retinal damage through ET‐1 and transforming growth β1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of SIRT1 and its role in the pathogenesis of diabetic micro‐ and macrovascular diseases.
the mechanisms underlying the protective role of SIRT in diabetes.
the regulation of SIRT1 and p300, which is important in diabetic complications, and the role of ET‐1 and/or TGF‐β as a mediator of SIRT1‐regulated diabetic complications.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in diabetes, hyperglycemia causes SIRT1 reduction and p300 up‐regulation.
in diabetes, SIRT1 down‐regulation causes endothelial injury through up‐regulation and activation of ET‐1 and p300‐mediated TGF‐β signalling.
SIRT1 over-expression in diabetes prevents ET‐1 and TGFB1 up-regulation in the kidney and retina, and thereby protects from the development of renal and retinal complications in diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SIRT1 over‐expression in diabetes may be a potential therapeutic approach to prevent renal and retinal complications in diabetes.
